review.notes:
Spoonjoy is the free native iPhone and iPad app for spoonjoy.app. Sign-in is required because recipes, cookbooks, cook logs and shopping lists live in the user's Spoonjoy account and sync with the website.

What makes Spoonjoy different from other recipe managers: every published recipe is a public page on spoonjoy.app (the Share button produces a link anyone can open); recipes can be forked with a permanent "forked from" credit to the original chef; each recipe shows Cooks, which are photo logs from everyone who cooked it; cook-mode progress (current step, scale, checked ingredients) syncs with the server, so it continues on another device or the website; and users can connect an AI assistant through Spoonjoy's MCP connector with OAuth access they can disconnect in Settings → Connections. There are no in-app purchases.

New in 1.2:
- Cook mode: open a recipe, tap Cook. One step fills the screen; on iPhone swipe to change step, on iPad use Back and Next. Close returns to where you started.
- Voice: in cook mode tap the mic, say "next", "back" or "repeat".
- Timer: check a timed step's last ingredient and its timer starts; it shows in the Dynamic Island and Lock Screen.
- Kitchen: Add a recipe (+) in the toolbar; Cooking now reopens a cook in progress.
- iPad: cook in two windows; each keeps its own cook.

Sign-in options (Guideline 4.8): Sign in with Apple is the first option on the sign-in screen on iPhone, iPad and Mac, above Continue with Google, Continue with GitHub and the email and password fields.

Demo account: enter the username and password provided in the email and password fields on the sign-in screen. It is Johnny Appleseed's kitchen: seven apple recipes (Honeycrisp Galette, Tarte Tatin, Waldorf Salad and more), the cookbooks "The Orchard" and "One More Thing", a recipe forked from Tim's Test Kitchen, cook logs from Tim, and a shopping list. Sign in with Apple also works and creates a new, empty kitchen.

Where to find key features:
- Fork credit: open "Brown Butter Apple Crumble, with pecans"; the credit line sits under the title. Recipe actions (···) → Fork to try it.
- Cooks: on any recipe, scroll to Cooks; tap Log to add one (optional photo).
- Cook mode and sync: open a recipe → Cook mode, check an ingredient, then open the same recipe on spoonjoy.app (same account) to see the same step and checks. A step with a duration and ingredients starts its timer when its last ingredient is checked; the timer and the current step show on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island.
- Voice: in cook mode, tap the microphone and say "next", "back", "repeat" or "timer". Recognition runs on the device.
- Shopping: Shopping tab; checkoff works offline. Send to Reminders asks for Reminders access so it can avoid duplicates.
- Siri and Shortcuts: "Start cooking in Spoonjoy", "Next step in Spoonjoy".
- AI features: restyling a cover or importing a recipe first shows a consent sheet naming the provider (Google Gemini or OpenAI) and what is sent. It can be turned off in Settings → Safety & privacy.
- Report and block: on any recipe or chef page, ··· → Report… or Block. Reported content is hidden for the reporter at once and reviewed within 24 hours; blocked chefs disappear from feeds, search and notifications. Manage blocks in Settings → Safety & privacy.
- Privacy policy, terms and support: Settings → About.
- Account deletion: Kitchen toolbar → account button → Settings → Delete account.

iPhone Duo: on the inner screen in landscape, a recipe becomes a two-page spread with its gutter on the hinge. Held tall and half-open (tabletop), cook mode splits at the fold: the step above, the checklist and controls below. iPad in landscape shows the same spread.

Contact: ari@spoonjoy.app

en-US.name: Spoonjoy: Recipes & Cookbooks
en-US.subtitle: Save, then cook step by step
en-US.promotionalText: Hands covered in dough and you need the next step? Say "next". Spoonjoy shows one step at a time, with only the ingredients that step needs.
en-US.description:
Spoonjoy keeps your recipes and walks you through cooking them, one big step at a time. It's free, with no ads and no subscription.

Paste a link and Spoonjoy imports the recipe, or type up the one your dad never wrote down. When it's time to make it, tap Cook. One step fills the screen with only the ingredients that step needs, set big enough to read from the stove.

COOK MODE
Cook mode listens. Say "next", "back", "repeat" or "timer". The mic is on only while cook mode is open, and your phone does the listening, not a server. Tick off the last ingredient of a timed step and its timer starts by itself. The countdown sits in the Dynamic Island and on the Lock Screen, and the screen stays on until you're done. After dark, cook mode turns warm and dim instead of bright white.

Start on your iPhone and finish on the iPad propped against the backsplash, or on spoonjoy.app. Your step, your scaling and the ingredients you ticked are already there.

FORK A RECIPE, KEEP THE CREDIT
Find a recipe you like in someone else's kitchen and fork it. You get your own copy to change, and a "forked from" line under the title names the cook you got it from. That line stays put, however much garlic you add.

COOK NOTES
Every time someone makes a recipe, they can log the cook with a photo and a note: "Doubled the lemon." "Needed ten more minutes at 375." The notes stay on the recipe for the next person, and for you next month. A good cook photo can become the recipe's cover.

COOKBOOKS
Gather recipes into your own cookbooks, like Weeknights or Sunday Baking, and share a whole cookbook with one link.

SHOPPING LIST
Add a recipe's ingredients to your list in one tap. Check things off by aisle, even with no signal at the back of the store. If your household runs on Reminders, Spoonjoy sends the list there without making duplicates.

ON THE WEB
Every recipe you publish has its own page on spoonjoy.app. Text the link to your sister and it opens in her browser. She doesn't need the app.

iPHONE DUO AND iPAD
Open an iPhone Duo flat and a recipe lies across both screens like a cookbook, ingredients on the left page and the method on the right. Stand it half-open and the step faces you while the checklist lies on the counter. iPad in landscape gets the same two-page spread.

MORE
- Siri: "Start cooking in Spoonjoy", "Next step in Spoonjoy", "Add to my Spoonjoy shopping list".
- Spotlight finds your recipes, cookbooks and shopping items.
- Connect an AI assistant to your kitchen. You approve what it can touch, and you can cut it off in Settings.

Sign in with Apple, Google, GitHub or an email and password, the same account you use on spoonjoy.app. You can report a recipe or block a chef from their page, and export your data or delete your account whenever you like.

Recipes, cookbooks and cook notes you publish are public. Your email, shopping list and sign-in details stay private.

Privacy policy: https://spoonjoy.app/privacy
Terms of service: https://spoonjoy.app/terms
